scope: Pinned-author-version method reproduction and all declared core simulation comparisons, including two verified execution corrections; not a certified original 2024 release.

primary_table1.reference_groups: acados and naive retain their original foothold-restored trajectory paths; the corrected adaptive pair consists of 100 new episodes.

supported_findings: All original three base methods complete 60 s Figure 3 tracking in the fixed +/-5 N/Nm reconstruction.
Corrected adaptive frequency increases under the 40 N push and returns to nominal; both compared controllers survive the declared 8 s reconstruction.
The corrected same-implementation frequency contrast improves 60 s no-fall outcomes from 0/50 to 22/50 and mean time without a fall from 7.93536 to 42.72 s; 48/50 paired seeds last longer.

Clock correction reduces >3 cm continuing-swing reference jumps from 71.83 percent to 0.206 percent. Its +4.70 s paired mean lifetime change has a 95 percent interval spanning zero; a reliable lifetime improvement from that correction alone is not established.
remaining_gap: The paper-specific strong-disturbance comparison is not fully explained: our declared Figure 4 reconstruction does not produce the acados fall, and the original Table I episode length, command, complete wrench schedule and scoring/configuration snapshot are unavailable in the selected paper/source. The new data establish frequency benefit and expose execution limits, but do not identify how much of the remaining difference comes from those unpublished conditions versus retained modern author implementation choices.
required_external_evidence: Original Figure 4 full velocity command, push timing and controller/helper configuration.
Original Table I episode duration, reset/phase settings, wrench generation/timing, failure definition, and controller/model parameter snapshot.
real_robot_status: Original Aliengo experiments unperformed; later H stage.
